L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: 392ce0e92e7fdc792f52b75331dd53ba08fc44f6

I ran `check-governed-merges --branch` at this head. It reads NOT governed: 0 of 7 paths are on the register, and the PR is 353 lines. The seat asked for a declaration-face L2 after this verdict. One landing note for the seat follows.

#### Must-fix
None.

#### Should-fix
None.

#### Landing note (seat)
- **`Fixes #35014` closes the card while item 4 has no card yet.**
  - Item 4 is the history list's per-app default, the All switch, and navigate-first.
  - It is split out by seat ruling and is right now only mailbox request 6966608417 on #32588 (route A: a cloud card, then an objectstack follow-up `Blocked-by` it).
  - I read the mailbox through 02:20Z and found no filed card number yet.
  - Before landing, confirm triage filed it, and cross-link it from #35014 so the closed card points forward.

#### What I checked
- **Shape and scope.**
  - `Fixes #35014` is present. Clause-② `no` and Metadata-protocol `none` match claim 6964657963.
  - All seven files are on the claim's surface: `ChatDockConversation.tsx`, `chatDockTarget.ts`, `useConsoleChatDock.tsx`, their colocated tests, and one changeset.
  - `chatScope.ts`, the `/ai` page and server storage are untouched, as the card requires.
  - The merge `fd7e3a13` is pure: `git show --remerge-diff` is empty.
  - There are no new UI strings, so no i18n keys are owed.
- **The fix matches the card's root cause.** On main, the drawer body took `target.packageId` over the app in view once any target existed (`ChatDockConversation.tsx:197`).
  - Now the host stamps each target with the app it was placed in (`placeDockTarget`, `app: <authorable package> | null`).
  - The host hands the body a target only where `dockTargetFollowsApp` holds: in the app it was opened in, or in the app it names.
  - So in another app the body gets no target, and resolves that app's ambient scope, as card item 1 asks.
- **The edge cases, read against the code.**
  - **Bind-on-create at Home.** `handlePackageBound` calls `onTargetChange` with `packageId: X`, and the page moves to X. The target is shown either way, because the `packageId === app` arm covers it. The layout-effect ref makes the stamp read X when the child's effect fires in the commit that changes the app. That holds because every layout effect of a commit runs before any passive effect.
  - **A fresh target naming its thread on first send** gets the current app's stamp. In another app it is withheld, so that effect does not fire there.
  - **An unplaced stored target** (an old `/ai…` link) is placed in the first app that reads it. The write-back effect then persists the stamp.
  - **Home and the built-in apps** both resolve to `null` through the shared `ambientAppPackage`. The body now uses the same resolver in place of its inline copy, so item 3 holds.
  - **Equality.** `sameDockTarget` now compares `app`, and the docblock says so.
- **Item 6, `ask`.** ui ADR-0057 Amendment A2 says "`ask` stays ambient". The pin asserts one ask thread in every app and no `app:PKG:ask` key.
  - No ADR text is made false by this PR. A2 already says switching the chip switches threads, and that each app gets its own build thread.
- **Tests.**
  - The new describe drives the real `useConsoleChatDock` host. On main 5 tests fail (blob-checked restore), and the ablation of the `shownTarget` gate fails the same 5.
  - The two preservation pins (the switcher, and `ask`) pass on main by design. The body says so.
  - The `ConsoleLayout.dockBinding` change only adds the `app` stamp to an expectation.
  - The dev reports 45/45 on the touched files and 1123/1123 across the 115 importer files, and declares that the full suite was left to CI.
- **Changeset.** `@object-ui/app-shell` patch. The package is private, but main carries the same precedent (e.g. `.changeset/32749-ai-chat-image-pdf-attachments.md`). Check Changeset is green.
- **CI on this head.** Every check-run's latest run concluded success or skipped:
  - Test UI (16 shards), Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, and the Lint and Type Check families.
  - The one PR-body guards failure (01:53Z) is superseded by a success at 01:54Z, after the body edit.
  - Merge state: clean.

#### Notes (nit-level, for the L2's declaration face)
- **N1.** The target is a single per-tab slot. Coming back to app A shows A's thread again through A's ambient `app:A:build` key, which is A's latest build thread. If the user picked an older history row in A, then opened another thread in B, A shows its latest thread rather than that row. The changeset's "Going back to the first app shows its thread again" is true for the plan-carrying latest thread, which is the card's acceptance line. It is not true for an arbitrary picked row.
- **N2.** An Ask selection made in app A is stamped with A. In app B the drawer falls back to B's ambient thread, not to Ask. The ask thread itself is unchanged and "one tap away", as the acceptance notes declare. That is the product choice not following the user, which is worth a line in the L2.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `392ce0e92e7fdc792f52b75331dd53ba08fc44f6`
Local-runs: none

What I read: card #35014 (its body and all 3 comments: triage 6964426585, claim 6964657963, dev report 6966577949), PR #35078 (its body and file list, the net diff against merge-base `357fb1ea45`, with 7 files, +340/-13), the PR comments (L1 ACCEPT 6967157277, contract-review claim 6967171206), #35081, and the 60 check-runs on the head. cloud#4835 returned 403 in this session, so I know it only through what #35081 says about it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: none moves.** No `packages/spec` schema, no metadata key, no server route, and no request body changes. The conversation create body and transport are not in the diff. `chatScope.ts` is untouched, so the scope keys `app:PKG:build`, `build` and `ask`, and the localStorage thread cache under them, stay byte-identical. Drafts and plans live under those keys, so none are re-keyed.
- **Stored per-tab state: one additive member.** This is right. The sessionStorage key `ai-chat-dock-target` (a per-tab key, not localStorage) gains an optional `app: string | null`.
  - **Forward.** A value written by a prior version has no `app`. It reads as "unplaced", and `placeDockTarget` stamps it with the first app it is read in. The write-back effect then persists the stamp. Nothing is dropped or misfiled. Pinned by "an old /ai… link opens its conversation in the app it lands in".
  - **Backward.** On a rollback, main's `readStoredDockTarget` and `compactTarget` copy only agent, conversationId, packageId and fresh, so the extra member is ignored.
  - **Upgrade.** An existing user's threads and drafts are not lost or misfiled after upgrade.
- **TS surface: additive.** `ChatDockTarget` (re-exported from `ui/packages/app-shell/src/index.ts:376`) gains an optional member. `chatDockTarget.ts` gains three exports: `ambientAppPackage`, `placeDockTarget` and `dockTargetFollowsApp`. `@object-ui/app-shell` is `"private": true`, so nothing is published, and no package outside app-shell imports `ChatDockTarget`.
- **`sameDockTarget` now also compares `app`.** This is right. Its docblock is updated, and only the host's dedupe and write-back call it.
- **`ChatDockConversation.tsx`** swaps its inline A2 predicate for the shared `ambientAppPackage`. The expression is identical (`appPackageId && !isPlatformBuiltinApp(...)`), so there is one resolver, as A2 requires ("There is no second resolver").
- **Root cause and fix match the card.** On main, the body took `target.packageId` over the app in view once any target existed. Now the host passes the body only a target that `dockTargetFollowsApp` accepts (`shownTarget`). In any other app the body sees no target and resolves that app's ambient scope. The ref is set in a layout effect, so a child's passive effect in the same commit reads the new app. That ordering argument holds.
- **ADR-0057 Amendment A2 holds.** A2 says "`ask` stays ambient": the key is the product alone for an `ask` dock. The diff writes no `app:PKG:ask` key. The ask pin asserts one ask thread across apps, with `app:app.notes:ask` null. A2's build-key rule ("`app:PKG:build` exactly when build and authorable") is untouched. The Studio-copilot sharing (same `app:PKG:build`) is pinned by "back in app A … on the key the Studio copilot reads", and the existing 10926 pins stay green. No ADR text is made false.
- **The new tests are real pins.**
  - The new describe in `ChatDock.appBinding-10926.test.tsx` drives the real host `useConsoleChatDock` through its own `control.open` handle and by re-rendering with another `appPackageId`, against the real drawer rail.
  - It asserts what the user sees: the chip text, the empty-state title, the request `context.packageId`, `conversationId`, and the localStorage scope keys.
  - Five pins exercise the new gate, and the dev reports them red on main (sources restored from `357fb1ea45`, blob-checked). Replacing the `shownTarget` gate with `target` turns the same 5 red.
  - The other two pins, the scope switcher (item 2) and `ask` (item 6), are preservation pins. They pass on main by design, and the PR body says so.
  - The unit pins in `chatDockTarget.test.tsx` cover every arm of `dockTargetFollowsApp`, `placeDockTarget` never re-stamping, the empty-target collapse, and the null round-trip through storage.
  - The `ConsoleLayout.dockBinding-10926` edit only adds the stamp to an existing expectation. No assertion was weakened.
- **Check-runs on the head (60): every latest run is success or skipped.**
  - Test UI and its shards, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI and Dogfood Regression Gate all succeeded.
  - The one PR-body guards failure (01:53:46Z) and the one cancelled Check Changeset (01:53:46Z) were both followed by a success at 01:54:45Z and 01:54:49Z, after the body edit.
  - Merge state: clean. The PR is still a draft.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/35014-ai-drawer-follows-app.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. This is right. The diff is a behaviour fix inside one private package, with an additive optional member on an internal type and no published surface. A patch matches the private-package changeset precedent on main, and Check Changeset is green on the head.
- Clause-②: no is right. No served contract changes: no request body, no route, no schema, no metadata key. No stored contract changes either: the localStorage scope and draft keys are untouched, and the one sessionStorage member is additive and readable both ways. The PR body, the changeset and claim 6964657963 all carry the same `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0] (how a history row learns its app; options A, B, C): answered.** The seat took route A.
  - #35081 was filed at 01:55:56Z with `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/cloud#4835`, labelled `pm:blocked`, `domain:ui` and `p2`.
  - It appears on #35014's timeline as a cross-reference at 01:55:57Z, so the closed card points forward. #35081 is not a GitHub sub-issue of #35014.
  - The card's own exit ("需要的话在 PR 里说明并另立 cloud 卡") is honoured: the PR's Acceptance notes give the measured reason (`ConversationListItem` carries no app, and the create sends `{}`).
- **open_questions[1] (Part of vs Fixes): answered with option B.** Item 4 now has its own card, and the PR body opens `Fixes #35014`. #35081's body states "PR #35078 ships items 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 and closes #35014". That is consistent.
- **should-fix S1: the PR body points item 4 at the wrong place.**
  - **The problem.** The 维护者速读 says "另立卡片（#32588）", and the Acceptance notes say "filed on #32588". #32588 is the `pm:mailbox`, not a card. The body's last edit (about 01:54Z) came before #35081 existed.
  - **The answer to the brief's question.** No, the PR body does not say item 4 went to #35081 or cloud#4835.
  - **Why it matters.** A maintainer reading the merged PR, or the card it closes, is pointed at a mailbox instead of the follow-up.
  - **Fix before landing.** Replace both "#32588" mentions with "#35081 (Blocked-by cloud#4835)". This touches no code and does not change the head's verdicts.
- **nit N1 (L1): single target slot.** On the declaration face it is a nit.
  - Back in app A, after a new target was set in B, A shows its ambient `app:A:build` latest thread rather than an older history row the user had picked there.
  - The card's acceptance line ("回到应用 A：A 的那一段还在，未发布的方案卡还在") is about the plan-carrying latest thread, and that is pinned.
  - The changeset's "Going back to the first app shows its thread again" reads slightly wider than that. The wording could say "its latest build thread". No contract effect.
- **nit N2 (L1): an Ask selection made in app A does not follow into app B.** On the declaration face it is a nit.
  - In app B the drawer shows B's ambient (default-agent) thread. A2's "`ask` stays ambient" governs the ask thread's key, and that key is unchanged: the same ask thread is one tap away in every app.
  - So A2 holds. The agent choice is per-target product behaviour, and the Acceptance notes declare it. Nothing to fix in this PR.
- **nit N3: a target stored before the upgrade can still show the old app's thread once.**
  - **The case.** A tab already holds a target that names `packageId: A`, stored by the old bundle while the user had already moved to app B (the bug state), and the user reloads in B after the deploy.
  - **What happens.** The target is placed in B and keeps showing A's thread in B, with the chip naming A (header and content agree), until the next target is set.
  - **Limits.** It happens once per tab and only in sessionStorage, and it does not lose data.
  - **Possible fix.** Stamping an unplaced target that names an authorable package with that package, rather than with the app in view, would close it. Not required for this card.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding.** The diff is client-side drawer state only. It adds no id materialisation, no in-app join, and no data query of any kind.
- **Dev flags.**
  - `out_of_scope_findings` (cloud: record the app per conversation) is now filed as cloud#4835, through #35081.
  - The dev report's note that the full app-shell suite was not run locally is answered by CI Test UI succeeding on this head.
  - No security findings were declared, and none are visible in the diff.
